name: Snowflake
description: Snowflake is a fully managed, cross-cloud data platform that separates storage and compute for data warehousing, data engineering, and AI application workloads, billed on a consumption basis.
best_for: Teams that want a warehouse-first cloud data platform with independently scalable storage and compute, credit-based consumption pricing, and built-in data sharing, rather than managing their own database infrastructure.
features: Multi-cluster, cross-cloud data warehouse with storage and compute billed and scaled independently
Snowpark for building data pipelines and applications in Python, Java, and Scala that run inside Snowflake
Openflow for moving and integrating data from external systems into Snowflake
Cortex AI for querying large language models and building generative AI features directly on governed data, plus vector search
Snowflake ML for centralized model development and MLOps from a single UI
Snowflake Notebooks and Streamlit support for building interactive data apps in Python
Data Clean Rooms and Snowflake Marketplace for privacy-preserving data sharing and access to thousands of third-party data listings
Horizon governance layer for built-in compliance, security, and access controls
pros: Storage and compute scale and bill independently, so idle compute doesn't add cost on top of stored data
30-day trial includes $400 of free usage credit to test real workloads, not just a stripped-down demo
Snowflake Marketplace gives direct access to thousands of third-party data listings without separate ETL work
cons: No published self-serve price list — per-credit rates depend on cloud, region, and edition and require the pricing calculator or a sales conversation
No perpetual free tier; after the 30-day/$400 trial ends, a credit card is required to continue

pricing.starting_price: Usage-based, billed per Snowflake credit consumed plus separate storage fees; no flat starting price is published

tiers.name: Standard
tiers.notes: Entry-level edition with core warehousing features, billed per Snowflake credit consumed plus separate storage charges.

tiers.name: Enterprise
tiers.notes: Adds multi-cluster warehouses and extended governance/security features; Snowflake's most commonly recommended edition.

tiers.name: Business Critical
tiers.notes: For regulated industries; adds Tri-Secret Secure encryption and enhanced disaster recovery.

tiers.name: Virtual Private Snowflake (VPS)
tiers.notes: A fully isolated Snowflake environment with Business Critical features in a dedicated deployment.

alternatives.name: Databricks
alternatives.description: A lakehouse platform unifying data engineering, SQL analytics, and machine learning on open formats like Delta Lake and Iceberg.
alternatives.best_for: Teams whose workloads lean heavily toward data engineering, ML/AI model development, and open-format lakehouse architecture rather than a pure SQL warehouse.
strengths: Open table format support (Delta Lake, Iceberg)
Runs natively on AWS, Azure, and GCP

faq.question: Does Snowflake have a free trial?
faq.answer: Yes. New accounts get a 30-day free trial with $400 in free usage credit, whichever runs out first.

faq.question: How is Snowflake priced?
faq.answer: Snowflake uses consumption-based pricing: compute is billed per Snowflake credit consumed (the rate depends on edition, cloud, and region) and storage is billed separately as a monthly fee based on average compressed data stored.

faq.question: What compliance certifications does Snowflake have?
faq.answer: Snowflake maintains ISO 27001 and SOC 2 Type II attestations, along with PCI DSS compliance and a HIPAA compliance report available to customers, among other certifications.
